claims.text: Ta-Nb-Mo-W-V is a refractory high-entropy alloy system.
The initial Ta-Nb-Mo-W-V alloy is a single-phase BCC solid.
The initial alloy exhibits severe local lattice distortion.
Full ab initio thermodynamic integration is prohibitively computationally expensive for this alloy.
A perturbation scheme driven by an MLP will be computationally faster than full ab initio thermodynamic integration.
Applicable empirical force fields are limited for high-entropy alloys.
Empirical EAM potentials fail to capture the complex liquid structure of multicomponent refractory alloys.
An MLP trained only on solid and high-temperature solid configurations will not generalize adequately to the liquid state.
The liquid occupies local-environment descriptor space absent from a solid-only MLP training set.
Omission of liquid configurations from training produces inaccurate liquid enthalpy and entropy.
Liquid configurations differ from solid configurations in long-range order and coordination statistics.
Poor liquid-state extrapolation by the solid-trained MLP artificially stabilizes the solid or otherwise biases the free-energy landscape.
The biased free-energy landscape can cause the perturbation scheme to converge to a false minimum.
TOR-TILD or a similar approach may fail in multicomponent systems because its training set inadequately samples the high-dimensional compositional space.
The solid-only MLP perturbation scheme will significantly underestimate the melting temperature.
The scheme will underestimate the solid-liquid free-energy difference.
The predicted liquid structure factor will contain spurious ordering absent from ab initio or experimental liquid structures.
The proposed failure mode is specific to multicomponent refractory HEAs whose MLP training sets omit liquid configurations.
The failure mode may not occur in simpler binary systems or when liquid environments are represented by the training data.
The magnitude of the melting-point bias depends on the structural difference between solid and liquid and on the MLP architecture.

contradictions.description: The mechanism invokes artificial stabilization of the solid, which would ordinarily extend solid stability and tend to raise the predicted melting temperature, whereas the predicted outcome specifies a lower melting temperature. No sign-resolved free-energy argument reconciles these directions.

The hypothesis refers generally to a biased estimate of liquid free energy, while the outcome alternates between underestimating melting temperature and underestimating an unsigned or sign-undefined solid-liquid free-energy difference. The necessary direction of the liquid free-energy error is not specified.
